newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares continue slide in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares continue slide in quiet trade.

text.p: Eyyptian share prices fell for the fourth day this week in quiet trade dominated by a large private deal in Suez Canal Bank.
The Capital Market Authority's all-share index slipped 2.66 points to a two-week low of 352.88 in below-average volume of 46.87 million pounds ($13.80 million).

A large private deal helped Suez Canal Bank generate 12.23 million pounds of the day's total turnover. Mohammed Abdullah, managing director of Intercapital brokerage, said the deal was for 80,000 shares and was probably a sale to a large investor as part of the government's privatisation programme.
"We are at a stage where retail clients are still leaving the market and are being replaced by institutions and more educated investors," Abdullah told Reuters.

"Retail clients see prices go down and panic and sell more, creating a snowball effect, and the educated investors are making use of the lower prices. But there is no fear in what's happening. It's very healthy because it's a way to prevent overpricing and investors are becoming more educated," he said.
The banking sector was the most solid performer in Wednesday's market, Abduallah said.

Misr International Bank/MIBANK rose nine pounds to 570, Export Development Bank of Egypt closed 2.5 pounds higher at 439.5, Mohandes Bank climbed 1.95 to 40.95, Egypt Arab African Bank/EAAB closed 1.64 pounds higher at 34.51.

Heliopolis Housing and Development closed 1.99 higher at 404 after trading in shares worth almost three million pounds but its housing sector stablemate Medinet Nasr Housing and Development slid 9.75 pounds to 230.
"There's no justification for this fall. It's purely technical. All the news coming out of Medinet Nasr is good," Abdullah said.

Two companies in the pharmaceutical sector generated relatively healthy volumes. Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries rose 2.75 pounds after trading in 2.58 million pounds while Hoechst Orient traded in shares worth 1.60 million pounds but it closed 0.57 pounds lower.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 485.42 points from 493.09 points on Tuesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 260.4 from 261.28 points.
Out of the 92 shares traded, 27 rose, 41 fell while 24 ended unchanged.
